title: Ghost Shark Uncrewed Submarine Shown Launching Aerial Drones For The First Time
summary: New video footage reveals Australia's Ghost Shark uncrewed submarine launching aerial drones from a 12-tube launcher. The video also shows two deployable masts, offering new insights into the UUV's multi-mission capabilities.
detail:
A new video has revealed Australia's Ghost Shark uncrewed underwater vehicle (UUV) demonstrating the capability to launch aerial drones from a 12-tube launcher and deploy two masts. This marks the first public display of this specific multi-domain functionality for the Ghost Shark.

This development is significant because it dramatically expands the operational utility of UUVs. By launching aerial drones from underwater, the Ghost Shark can extend its sensor reach far beyond its immediate vicinity, potentially acting as a stealthy forward scout, a communications relay, or even a localized attack platform. This capability introduces a new dimension to multi-domain warfare, allowing a submerged platform to influence the air and surface domains, thereby enhancing situational awareness, target acquisition, and overall battlefield effectiveness without exposing crewed assets.

The Ghost Shark, developed by Anduril Australia, is part of a global trend towards integrating autonomous systems into naval warfare. It aims to increase naval mass, reduce risk to personnel, and provide new tactical options. The ability to deploy aerial assets from a UUV represents a significant technological leap, blurring the lines between traditional operational domains and potentially reshaping how naval forces conduct complex missions.

title: Navy F/A-18 Super Hornet Spotted Carrying New AIM-174B And AIM-260 Long-Range Missiles Together
summary: A U.S. Navy F/A-18 Super Hornet from VX-31 was observed carrying both the new AIM-174B and AIM-260 long-range missiles simultaneously. This sighting provides an early glimpse of future fleet weapon configurations, with the AIM-424 Malice also expected to join.
detail:
A U.S. Navy F/A-18 Super Hornet was recently photographed carrying both the new AIM-174B and AIM-260 Joint Advanced Tactical Missiles (JATM) simultaneously. The report also mentioned the AIM-424 Malice, indicating a suite of new air-to-air weapons.

This sighting is crucial as it signals that these advanced long-range air-to-air missiles are nearing operational deployment with the fleet. The AIM-260 JATM is a critical next-generation missile designed to counter advanced adversary aircraft and their long-range air-to-air missiles, particularly those developed by China and Russia, aiming to surpass the range and capabilities of the current AIM-120 AMRAAM. The AIM-174B is likely a variant of the AIM-174, a modified Standard Missile-6 (SM-6) adapted for air-to-air use, offering extreme range. Carrying both suggests a layered approach to air combat, providing pilots with diverse engagement options against different threats at varying ranges, thereby enhancing the Super Hornet's lethality and survivability in contested airspace.

The U.S. military is in a race to maintain air superiority against peer competitors who have developed increasingly capable long-range air-to-air missiles. The AIM-260 is specifically developed to address this 'missile gap,' ensuring U.S. fighters can engage targets at greater distances. The simultaneous carriage of these advanced weapons signifies a strategic move to equip existing platforms with cutting-edge capabilities to counter evolving threats.

title: OCIUS’ New Bluebottle Hybrid USV Demonstrates Capability at Maritime Big Play Pacific
summary: Ocius' new diesel-hybrid Bluebottle Uncrewed Surface Vessel (USV) is participating in the US Navy-led Maritime Big Play Pacific exercise. This marks the first time the Bluebottle Hybrid, which carries ThayerMahan sensors, has been involved in a Navy exercise.
detail:
OCIUS’ new Bluebottle Hybrid Uncrewed Surface Vessels (USVs), which combine renewable power with diesel engines, recently participated in the US Navy-led Maritime Big Play Pacific exercise. This marked their first involvement in a Navy exercise, where they carried specialized ThayerMahan payloads.

This participation is significant as it demonstrates the growing integration of autonomous surface vessels into major naval operations. These hybrid USVs offer extended endurance and operational flexibility due to their dual power sources, making them ideal for long-duration missions such as intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR), anti-submarine warfare (ASW), or maritime domain awareness. Their ability to carry specialized payloads, often acoustic sensors or other ISR equipment, highlights their potential as persistent, cost-effective sensor platforms. This reduces the need for larger, more expensive crewed vessels in certain roles, freeing them for higher-end missions and reducing risk to personnel.

Naval forces worldwide are heavily investing in uncrewed systems to augment their fleets. The 'hybrid' aspect of the Bluebottle is key, addressing the limitations of purely renewable systems in adverse conditions or when higher speeds are required, while still maximizing fuel efficiency. Exercises like Maritime Big Play Pacific are crucial for testing these technologies in realistic environments, refining tactics, and demonstrating interoperability between allied forces and new autonomous platforms.

title: EDGE Leads Integration of Sovereign Autonomous Systems in UAE Navy Demonstration with Allied Forces
summary: UAE's EDGE Group led the integration of sovereign autonomous systems for a UAE Navy demonstration of unmanned maritime capabilities, conducted with the U.S. Navy. EDGE provided planning, facilities, and operational assets, with specialists working alongside both navies.
detail:
UAE-based defense conglomerate EDGE Group led the integration of its sovereign autonomous systems for a UAE Navy demonstration of national and allied unmanned maritime capabilities. The exercise involved the United States Navy, with EDGE providing planning expertise, host facilities, and operational assets, and specialists working alongside both navies.

This event is significant as it showcases the UAE's increasing capability and ambition in developing and integrating advanced autonomous maritime systems. By leading such a demonstration with a major naval power like the U.S., EDGE and the UAE Navy are highlighting their indigenous technological advancements and their commitment to modernizing their forces with unmanned platforms. It also underscores the growing trend of international collaboration in autonomous warfare, where allied forces test interoperability and shared operational concepts. For the UAE, this represents a step towards greater strategic autonomy in defense technology, reducing reliance on foreign suppliers for critical capabilities. For the U.S. and other allies, it offers an opportunity to integrate new partners and systems into a broader network for maritime domain awareness and response.

Unmanned maritime systems (UMS) are a cornerstone of future naval strategies globally, offering advantages in persistence, cost-effectiveness, and risk reduction. Nations are increasingly seeking to develop 'sovereign' capabilities in this domain. Collaborative exercises are vital for developing common standards, testing interoperability, and building trust among allied forces operating these complex systems.

title: US Marine Corps makes Maven available service-wide
summary: The U.S. Marine Corps has made the AI-enabled battlefield management system, Maven, available service-wide. This deployment allows all commands and organizations within the service to utilize the system.
detail:
The U.S. Marine Corps has made Project Maven, an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled battlefield management system, available to all commands and organizations within the service.

This widespread deployment marks a significant step in integrating AI directly into the daily operational fabric of the Marine Corps. Project Maven, initially focused on using AI to process vast amounts of drone footage and other intelligence data to identify objects and patterns faster than humans, is now expanding its utility across the entire service. This means AI will be used to enhance situational awareness, accelerate decision-making, improve targeting, and potentially streamline logistics and planning. By automating data analysis and providing predictive insights, Maven aims to give Marines a critical advantage in complex, fast-paced combat environments, reducing cognitive load on personnel and enabling more effective responses.

Project Maven was launched by the Department of Defense in 2017 to accelerate the adoption of AI and machine learning. Its service-wide availability within the Marine Corps reflects a broader military push to leverage AI for 'decision advantage' – the ability to make better decisions faster than an adversary. This move is part of a larger strategy to modernize military capabilities, enhance data-driven operations, and prepare for future conflicts where information superiority and rapid adaptation will be paramount.
